newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB says blizzard likely stalls Red River seeding.
newsitem.headline: CWB says blizzard likely stalls Red River seeding.

text.p: A blizzard that dumped 57.4 cm (23 inches) on the Red River Valley will probably delay spring seeding by a couple of weeks, Canadian Wheat Board said.
"The blizzard that pounded southern Manitoba this weekend will likely push back spring seeding by a couple of weeks," CWB said in a statement.
The average date on which spring seeding begins across the Prairies is May 7, the CWB has said.
"With the additional snow and cool temperatures forecast for the coming week, the spring melt has been significantly delayed," the CWB said.
"Areas west of Portage-la-Prairie and Brandon (Manitoba), however, received smaller amounts of snow and the storm will not affect spring seeding," it said.
The weekend's blizzard broke four records and forced a revision to Manitoba Natural Resources' flood forecast due later this week. The Red River began rising in Winnipeg Tuesday.
